data.title: Typing React patterns
data.subtitle: Props, generics, useState trap, refs, events

cards.front: How should component props be typed?
cards.meaning: Props are a normal object type, usually an interface. Optional props use `?`. Runtime defaults live in the destructuring (`variant = 'primary'`), not in the type as default values.
cards.example: function Button({ label, onPress, variant = 'primary', children }: ButtonProps)

cards.front: ReactNode vs ReactElement vs string for children?
cards.meaning: ReactNode is anything React can render: elements, strings, numbers, arrays, null, undefined, booleans (mostly ignored). Prefer it for children. ReactElement is a single element only. Use string when children must be text-only.

cards.front: Why type variant as 'primary' | 'secondary' instead of string?
cards.meaning: Union literals make typos and invalid variants compile errors. string only fails at runtime (wrong CSS class).

cards.front: Does variant?: in the props type set a runtime default?
cards.meaning: No. Optional `?` only allows omitting the prop. Defaults belong in destructuring (`variant = 'primary'`), not only in the type.
cards.notes: Putting default prop values only in the type is a common mistake.

cards.front: How does List<T> stay typed without any in renderItem?
cards.meaning: T is inferred from items: T[] and checked against renderItem and keyExtractor. Callers rarely write List<User>. any on renderItem throws the item type away.
string — the literal widens. Invalid statuses will not be caught. For a closed set, pass an explicit type argument: useState<'idle' | 'loading' | 'success' | 'error'>('idle').

cards.front: Why does useState widen string/number/boolean literals?
cards.meaning: If TS inferred status as the literal 'idle', then setStatus('loading') would be a type error. Inference widens those literals so the setter is usable.

cards.front: When should useState stay string vs a status union?
cards.meaning: Closed set of states: pass an explicit type argument. Open text (useState('') for an input): plain string is correct.

cards.front: How do discriminated union actions type a reducer?
cards.meaning: A discriminant like type narrows in switch so action.by exists only on increment/decrement, not on reset. useReducer then types dispatch to accept only valid Actions.

Null-initialized element ref: React fills .current with the DOM node (or null). .current may be null until mount and after unmount. Interviews want this intent, not the RefObject vs MutableRefObject name.

cards.front: What does useRef(0) mean vs a DOM ref?
cards.meaning: Mutable-box ref: you read/write .current yourself (timerId, previous props). It persists across renders without re-render. Changing .current does not update the UI.

It exposes an inner DOM node (or child handle) to parents so they can hold a ref to the inner input, not just the wrapper. React 19 can pass ref as a normal prop in some setups; still know the classic generic order.

cards.front: What is the type-parameter order of forwardRef?
cards.meaning: forwardRef<RefType, PropsType> — ref element type first, props second. Easy trap to swap them.

cards.front: How do you type React DOM event handlers?
cards.meaning: Use React event generics, not a bare DOM Event: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> for input onChange, FormEvent<HTMLFormElement> for submit, MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement> for click. That ties e.target / e.currentTarget to the element.

cards.front: Must you annotate event handler parameters in JSX?
cards.meaning: No. Inline handlers can omit the annotation if the JSX prop context infers the type.
